Thanks for the context, Priyom / Lucia. High-level legal position (drafted for commercial):

1) Baseline: Redwood will indemnify and defend claims alleging third-party IP infringement to the extent the claim arises from Redwood-provided software (i.e., code or model artifacts we deliver). For customer-provided artifacts (models, tokenizers, plugins) we can offer a limited indemnity only where the customer provides the required evidence and cooperates in defense.

2) Open-source components: we cannot accept broad liability for open-source components that are publicly available and not created or modified by Redwood. For those, propose a carveout: Redwood excludes indemnity for third-party claims to the extent they arise solely from (i) public open-source components used without modification, or (ii) customer modifications of such components.

3) Defense/Control: where we do accept defense, we propose a joint-defense model: Redwood reserves the right to assume control of defense with customer consent; otherwise, Redwood may appoint counsel and seek cost-sharing if the claim is outside the scope of Redwood's obligations.

4) Evidence threshold: to trigger indemnity for customer-supplied artifacts, Redwood requires: SCA report (matching hashes/versions), provenance (commit hashes or release IDs), and a reasonable remediation window. Without those, we will reserve rights.

5) Caps and exclusions: propose standard MSA cap tied to the order form (e.g., lesser of fees paid in 12 months or X) and express carveouts for extraordinary damages, and for claims resulting from customer data misuse.

Lucia — can you confirm how often you run SCA and whether you can provide commit hashes for the model checkpoints? That will help us move to a short paragraph we can put in the Order Form. Grace — commercial is critical: procurement wants a single-sentence commitment they can accept; we should aim for a concise fallback position.

I'll prepare a redline (redline_MSA_v3.docx) with suggested language for the MSA/Order Form and highlight the paragraph numbers.

-Kim
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks team — commercial gist for procurement:
- OpenHealth needs an operationally simple answer. They cannot accept an open-ended carveout without a remediation path.
- Suggest we offer: (i) defense for third-party IP claims for Redwood-delivered assets; (ii) for customer-supplied artifacts (including customer-hosted models or tokenizers), provide defense only if customer supplies SCA report and provenance (commit hashes) and grants Redwood limited remediation rights; (iii) if claim arises solely from public open-source code not modified by Redwood, that is excluded.
- If procurement insists on a narrower carveout, ask for: (a) a lower deductibility / smaller cap for indemnity for OOT (out-of-tree) claims or (b) acceptance of a time-limited indemnity (e.g., 12 months post-deployment) for such claims.

Lucia — will procurement accept the evidence ask (SCA + hashes)? If yes, I can have a commercial note ready by Friday. If they push back, we may need a one-off escalation to Legal + Revenue Ops for an exception.

Cheers,
